luke.15.p1.b1.text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.

luke.15.p1.b2.text: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”

luke.15.p1.b3.text: Then Jesus told them this parable:

luke.15.p2.b1.text: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them,

luke.15.p2.b2.text: does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?

luke.15.p2.b3.text: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,

luke.15.p3.b1.text: ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’

luke.15.p3.b2.text: In the same way, I tell you that there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents

luke.15.p3.b3.text: than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.

luke.15.p4.b1.text: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them

luke.15.p4.b2.text: does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?

luke.15.p4.b3.text: ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’

luke.15.p4.b4.text: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”

luke.15.p5.b1.text: “There was a man who had two sons.

luke.15.p5.b2.text: ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’

luke.15.p5.b3.text: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country,

luke.15.p5.b4.text: where he squandered his wealth in wild living.

luke.15.p6.b1.text: After he had spent all he had,

luke.15.p6.b2.text: a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.

luke.15.p6.b3.text: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.

luke.15.p6.b4.text: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.

luke.15.p7.b1.text: Finally he came to his senses and said,

luke.15.p7.b2.text: ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food? But here I am, starving to death!

luke.15.p7.b3.text: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

luke.15.p7.b4.text: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’

luke.15.p8.b1.text: So he got up and went to his father.

luke.15.p8.b2.text: But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion.

luke.15.p8.b3.text: He ran to his son, embraced him,

luke.15.p9.b1.text: ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

luke.15.p9.b2.text: But the father said to his servants,

luke.15.p9.b3.text: ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him.

luke.15.p9.b4.text: Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.

luke.15.p10.b1.text: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.

luke.15.p10.b2.text: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’

luke.15.p11.b1.text: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.

luke.15.p11.b2.text: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.

luke.15.p11.b3.text: ‘Your brother has returned,’ … ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’

luke.15.p12.b1.text: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

luke.15.p12.b2.text: ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours.

luke.15.p12.b3.text: Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.

luke.15.p12.b4.text: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’

luke.15.p13.b1.text: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ … ‘and all that is mine is yours.

luke.15.p13.b2.text: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”
